$comment: The citations we are allowed to print (#464). Every objective a session cites must appear
here byte-identical, and scripts/standards-lint.mjs enforces that.
Why this file exists. `standards[].text` is published statutory wording that we QUOTE to a
teacher so she can justify a lesson to her head. A quote that drifts is worse than no quote:
it cites something no government ever published, and it does so in the one place we asked her
to trust us. Unlike the founder's own copy, which scripts/verbatim-fidelity.mjs holds against
its source rows, an external citation had no source to check against — so nothing could catch
a paraphrase. Three had already drifted in a single pack before this file existed:
'observe changes across the four seasons'  -> statutory text uses the numeral, '4 seasons'
K-ESS3-1 'plants or animals'               -> published text reads 'plants and animals'
Adding an entry is a research task, not a typing task. Fetch the published source, copy the
wording exactly, and record where and when it was read. Never add an entry from memory, and
never adjust an entry to match a session — the citation is the fixed thing; the mapping is
England publishes no per-objective codes. The programme of study carries none; 'Sc2/2.1a'
style codes come from commercial schemes numbering the statute themselves. So `code` here is
the real addressable unit: the year and the statutory subheading. Several objectives share a
code, which is correct and is why entries are matched on code and text together.

england.title: National curriculum in England: science programmes of study
england.scope: The statutory bullets only. The non-statutory guidance beside them is not citable. Working scientifically is statutory too and is published per key stage, not per year, so it is cited as "Key stage 1 · Working scientifically" and "Years 3 and 4 · Working scientifically" (the statute's "Lower key stage 2 – years 3 and 4"); those bullets and Year 4 living things were read 2026-09-07.

ngss.title: Next Generation Science Standards, performance expectations
ngss.scope: The performance expectation sentence as published. Clarification statements are not carried.

england-art-and-design.title: National curriculum in England: art and design programmes of study
england-art-and-design.scope: The key stage 1 statutory bullets only. Cited under system "england" with the code "Key stage 1 · Art and design", because the subject publishes no per-year subheadings.

england-english.title: National curriculum in England: English programmes of study
england-english.scope: The statutory spoken language bullets for years 1 to 6 only. Cited under system "england" with the code "Years 1 to 6 · Spoken language", the span the statute itself gives them.

england-mathematics.title: National curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study
england-mathematics.scope: The statutory bullets only. Cited under system "england" with the year and the statutory subheading, "Year 2 · Statistics", the same shape as science.

england-design-and-technology.title: National curriculum in England: design and technology programmes of study
england-design-and-technology.scope: The key stage 1 statutory bullets only. Cited under system "england" with the code "Key stage 1 · Design and technology", because the subject publishes no per-year subheadings.
